item.title: Healthy Food and Sustainable Consumption: What Do We Know and Where to Next?
item.content:encoded:
Natalina Zlatevska, University of Technology Sydney

Aya Aboelenien, HEC Montréal

Søren Askegaard, University of Southern Denmark

Belinda Barton, Bond University

Liisa Lähteenmäki, Aarhus University

Carolina Werle, Grenoble Ecole de Management

Food consumption intersects with critical challenges including diet-related health issues, environmental sustainability, and inequality. Marketing influences consumer choices through information, pricing, interventions, and cultural meanings. Research has examined approaches like labelling, nudges, and reformulation, but these studies have developed separately across disciplines, leaving gaps in understanding how interventions interact and scale.

This special issue integrates perspectives from consumer behaviour, public health, economics, and sustainability to develop a comprehensive understanding of how marketing can support healthier and more sustainable food systems. It emphasizes the broader systems in which consumption occurs, including families, social networks, cultural practices, firms, policy structures, and value chains.

The issue welcomes empirical and conceptual research, reviews, and meta-analyses that bridge theory with practical implications for policy, industry, and society. Priority is given to interdisciplinary work examining intervention effectiveness, government policy, labelling, product reformulation, consumer adaptation, equity, and structural barriers.

Appel publié par European Journal of Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Nudges and behavioural interventions for healthy and sustainable food consumption
  • Government policies and regulatory interventions
  • Food labelling and information disclosure
  • Product reformulation and industry responses
  • Trade-offs between health and environmental sustainability
  • Equity, access and unintended consequences
  • Consumer resistance and long-term behaviour change
  • Family influence and intergenerational food practices
  • Food consumption in households, communities and social networks
  • Food value chains and structural barriers
  • Consumer culture and food-related practices
  • Marketplace ideologies and cultural politics of health and sustainability

  • February 28, 2027: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
